title: CHAIN GAMES boot loader
summary: The platform's loading screen: the CHAIN GAMES logo builds in from a spritesheet while a hairline bar tracks real asset progress — but the bar can never top out before the logo has finished. First thing on screen in every generated game.

status.devBuild: ABSENT — the dev build shows no loading screen at all today
status.severity: must exist before anything else renders; it is stage 1 of FLOW.md

notPerGame: This is platform branding, not a skin. There is no per-game title, no per-game colour ramp and no per-game bar tint — an earlier revision had those and they were removed on purpose. If per-game boot theming is ever wanted again it belongs on the bar colour, never on a title.

container.where: inside the game-canvas container only (the generator's game iframe) — never over the host/studio chrome

logo.padContent: copies of the last frame, so the one-shot lands on the finished lockup
logo.playback: ONE-SHOT then hold — it is a logo build-in, not a spinner and not a cycle
logo.renderScale: 1:1, a 250px sheet frame in a 250px box; never upscaled
logo.marginRationale: the logo's ink ends at 57.8% of the frame, leaving 105px of transparent tail; 105 dead + 18 flex gap - 108 margin = a ~15px optical gap to the bar

stepping.why: background-position on a large sheet forces a re-rasterisation every step; it stuttered badly while the real assets were decoding alongside it
stepping.split: a transform animation cannot drive both axes on one element — the ROW walks on the wrapper, the COLUMN on the strip inside it
stepping.whyJumpNone: plain steps(8) divides into eighths while an 8-column sheet sits on sevenths of the travel — every rendered frame becomes two half-frames drifting further out of register, which looks garbled and too fast

logo.sizeBudget: keep the sheet small. An earlier 4092x4092 bake was 16.7 MP (~67 MB decoded) for a mark that renders at 250px and it visibly lagged; 2000x2000 is 4.0 MP / 228 KB.

bar.look: ultra-clean: a hairline, no glow, no colour ramp, no LOADING label

clockGate.rule: THE BAR MUST NOT REACH FULL BEFORE THE LOGO HAS FINISHED PLAYING
clockGate.implementation: width = real progress; max-width = a keyframe ramping 0% -> 100% over the loader's own 4.2667s (linear, fill both). A percentage max-width resolves against the track, so the two compose into exactly min(realProgress, playhead).
clockGate.behaviour: whichever is slower wins, in both directions — the bar can never outrun the logo, and a cold cache still holds it back on genuine loading
clockGate.whyCss: a per-frame JS clock would re-render on every frame and compete with the asset decoding this screen exists to cover
clockGate.symptomIfIgnored: on a warm cache the bar snaps to 100% in a few hundred ms and then sits there while the lockup assembles — it reads as if the game were waiting on nothing

progressTracking.rule: only critical jobs are tracked into the fraction; everything else is fired unawaited so it can never hold the bar back — it streams in behind the intro

exit.startsAt: max(criticalJobsSettled, LOADER_MS + BAR_HOLD_MS) measured from boot start
exit.holdRationale: the screen must dwell a beat on 'logo standing, bar full' before it goes
exit.armsNext: showGameIntro() is called before the fade, so the game intro's iris-from-black is already in progress when the overlay clears — no flash of empty canvas
exit.doNotDismissOnAssetsAlone: without the floor a warm cache tore the logo away mid-build; it read as a broken flicker, not a fast load

verification: Sample a fresh boot every ~250 ms and assert two things: (1) every sampled sheet offset is an exact multiple of the frame size on BOTH axes — a non-multiple means the steps() timing is off-grid; (2) the bar first reads 100% no earlier than the sample in which the sheet reaches its last cell. Our production run: bar 94.1% while the sheet was on cell [7,4], 100% on the sample where it reached [7,7].
